summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 (a general-release Mythos-class model) and Claude Mythos 5 (an unrestricted version for trusted cyber-defense and biology partners), both priced at $10/$50 per million tokens, with new safety classifiers, a 30-day data retention policy, and a brief suspension and redeployment of access shortly after launch.

mechanisms.reason: Anthropic states Fable 5 exceeds all previously generally-available models and is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability, showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas.

mechanisms.reason: The model is described as maintaining performance across millions of tokens and using persistent file-based memory, increasing memory/cache demands per serving instance.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 stays focused across millions of tokens in long-running tasks and improves its outputs using its own notes.

mechanisms.reason: Access to the newly launched models was suspended for customers days after release, directly reducing served inference volume during that period.
mechanisms.quote: We are suspending access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. We apologize for this disruption to our customers and are working to restore access as soon as possible.

practices.reason: Engineering teams building on Claude would treat this as a substantial capability upgrade across coding, reasoning and vision tasks, backed by stated benchmark and customer results.
practices.quote: Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability, showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas.

practices.reason: Named third-party benchmarks (FrontierCode, Finance Benchmark) and Anthropic's own red-teaming/jailbreak evaluations offer measurement approaches a team could adapt to assess model quality and safety, though the results are largely the lab's or partners' own unreplicated tests.
practices.quote: on Cognition’s FrontierCode evaluation, which tests whether models can pass difficult coding tasks while meeting the standards of high-quality production codebases, Fable 5 scores highest among frontier models, even at medium effort.

practices.reason: A dated change to subscription-plan access requires teams to plan for a switch to usage credits or degraded availability after June 22.
practices.quote: On June 23, we’ll remove Fable 5 from those plans. Using it after that will require usage credits .

notable_reason: A frontier-class model release with new government-linked restricted-access tier and safety classifiers was followed within days by a suspension and later redeployment of access, an unusual operational disruption worth tracking.
